title: Hawaii ex parte renewal share, August 2026
question: What percentage of Hawaii Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries due for renewal in August 2026 will CMS report as renewed on an ex parte basis in its first publication of the original (O), unadjusted submission?
resolutionSource: CMS, State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov)
resolutionRule: Resolves to Hawaii's August 2026 reporting-period original (O) submission row in CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c when CMS first publishes it. Compute 100 times Beneficiaries Whose Coverage Was Renewed on an Ex Parte Basis divided by Beneficiaries with a Renewal Due, using the numerator and denominator as first published, rounded to one decimal. Subsequent updated submissions and revisions do not change resolution.
drivers: Persistence of Hawaii's latest original-submission rate
Recent recovery within a lower 2026 level
Automated eligibility matching and reporting classification
New adult renewal requirements begin in 2027

reasoning.text: Hawaii August 2026 ex parte renewal share

The target is Hawaii's state row for August 2026, using original O submissions and first publication. All historical anchors use that same submission variant. The ledger does not explicitly name the denominator field; CMS's state renewal table defines its ex parte percentage against total beneficiaries due for renewal, which is the denominator used here. Historical shares are calculated from fetched counts; the current dataset's O rows are not independently archived publication-day vintages.

reasoning.call: GET https://data.medicaid.gov/api/1/datastore/query/5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c/0 with state_abbreviation=HI, original_or_updated=O, reporting_period>=202501 and reporting_period<=202506; echo the JSON response.

GET https://data.medicaid.gov/api/1/datastore/query/5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c/0 with state_abbreviation=HI, original_or_updated=O, reporting_period>=202507 and reporting_period<=202512; echo the JSON response.
GET https://data.medicaid.gov/api/1/datastore/query/5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c/0 with state_abbreviation=HI, original_or_updated=O and reporting_period>=202601; echo the JSON response.
Open https://www.medicaid.gov/resources-for-states/downloads/eligib-oper-and-enrol-snap-jun2026.pdf and inspect page 31, Coverage Retention and Disenrollment Rates by State.
reasoning.result: CMS's June 2026 Hawaii table reports 36,142 beneficiaries due for renewal, 88% renewed, 9% disenrolled, 3% pending and 74% renewed ex parte. Its heading explicitly expresses percentages against total beneficiaries due. The PDF uses whole-percent rounding; the API counts yield 74.478446%, or 74.5% at the target's precision.

reasoning.text: Schedule verification limitation: the fetched official CMS snapshot page lists June 2026 released September 25, 2026, and earlier completed releases. No applicable official announcement or calendar confirming August 2026 publication on December 15, 2026 was found. The required exact-date verification could not be satisfied. The resolutionDate remains 2026-12-15 solely because it is the supplied ledger contract; it is not represented as a verified CMS release date.

The reference class contains 18 fetched monthly original submissions. The outside-view base rate for the latest 12 months, July 2025 through June 2026, averages 71.707475%; January-June 2026 averages 67.667948%. The latest three months average 71.830113%. June's 74.478446% captures the recent recovery while remaining below June 2025's 85.492186%.

Level: anchor on June's latest original rate. Momentum: apply no additional trend adjustment because recent recovery conflicts with the longer decline. One-off effects: apply no adjustment, given empty recent Hawaii ex parte footnotes. Policy mechanism: Hawaii's fetched Med-QUEST page places new six-month adult renewals and work requirements at January 1, 2027, so assign no direct effect from those requirements to August 2026.

Prior/update/interval: use a latest-level persistence prior, with July 2025-June 2026 as the dispersion sample. Point = 100*26918/36142 = 74.478446%, with momentum, one-off and policy adjustments each zero. The 11 successive unrounded percentage-point changes have mean -1.009071 and centered sum of squares 485.329520. sigma = 6.966560 percentage points, calculated as sqrt(485.329520/10). The one-month 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 8.917196. For the two-month June-to-August horizon, multiply by sqrt(2), giving 12.610820, or 1.414 times the one-month width. Bounds = 74.478446 +/- 12.610820 = 61.867626 to 87.089266; rounded point and bounds are 74.5%, 61.9% and 87.1%.

Upside risk: stronger automated eligibility matching or a cohort especially suitable for ex parte renewal could raise the share. Downside risk: less suitable cohorts or classification of automated renewals as form-based renewals could lower it. The observed June-August 2025 decline was 8.698585 percentage points; repeating it would imply about 65.8%, inside the interval. A major matching-system disruption could land below 61.9%, outside the interval; processing predominantly automation-ready cases could land above 87.1%, outside the interval.
